findings.issue: The detach invariant (a client disconnect cannot spend an approval without sending RunAgent) is not protected by any listed test. Deleting the tokio::spawn from continue_run leaves every listed test green.
findings.evidence: The declared helper is `async fn consume_then_launch<C: ApprovalConsumer, T>(consumer: &C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T)`. It borrows the consumer, so it cannot spawn itself, and the spawn sits only in continue_run. The planned test a_dropped_handler_cannot_spend_an_approval_without_dispatching drops the outer future 'once the consumer has answered won'. In that helper nothing is awaited between the consumer answering and launch() running, so the launch is guaranteed once the future is polled after the answer. The test passes with no spawn. The real hazard is a drop during the consume RPC, when the server has committed but the client future is cancelled. The ordering scan (preflight < consume_then_launch < agentic_run_stream) does not look for a spawn. Fix: put the spawn and oneshot in a testable function such as spawn_consume_then_launch, with an owned consumer. Test it by dropping the receiver while the fake consumer is mid-await and committing server-side. Add a source scan that continue_run contains `tokio::spawn(`.

findings.issue: As specified, the guard cannot pass. It requires every executor-sourced token in CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS to appear in executor or session-core source, but some listed tokens are made by the gateway or do not exist yet.
findings.evidence: The design puts approval_not_found in the 16 tokens 'from the executor'. Session-core's NotFound text is 'approval not found for this run', and classify_continue_dispatch_failure turns every NotFound into approval_not_found, so the token is gateway-made. A grep of execution-core/src and session-core/src finds no `approval_not_found`, `continue_in_progress`, `continue_space_scope_unsupported` or `resume_checkpoint_unavailable`. Also note that classifying every NotFound as approval_not_found mislabels an executor-side NotFound, for example from authorize_run.

findings.issue: The 'a continuation never tells the client to retry' rule covers only the dispatch-failure frames. Frames built from a received RunAgentResponse still say retryable: true for a continuation whose approval is already spent. The SPA effect table says every frame code is retryable false, but only for the 19 listed codes.
findings.evidence: In agentic_run_stream the Failed outcome emits agent_run_failed with retryable: true. The Unknown outcome emits agent_run_state_unknown with retryable: true. The missing-output case emits agent_run_output_unavailable with retryable: true. Subscription failures use their own retry hints. None of these is in the design's changed set, and none is in the 19-code vocabulary. A new /continue after any of them gets 409 at preflight. Fix: either pass the retryable flag through the same resume-aware helper (retryable false when resuming), or state in the contract and the effect table that these frames are outside the closed set and must not be treated as retriable for chat.run.continue.

findings.file: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/run_service_grpc.rs and the binding requirement on RunDetail.resumable
findings.issue: The binding requirement says RunDetail.resumable and park_reason are service-readable only. The design keeps resumable readable by every reader at RPC level and reads it with the user bearer, and leaves any gating to an open question. If that gating were added, resume_mode_for would silently send 'segment' forever.
findings.evidence: At HEAD, row_to_detail sets resumable for any viewer who can read the run, and only park_reason is gated by may_read_park_reason (owner or service). The gateway's GetRun in continue_run uses authenticated_session_request with the user's model_bearer. The design admits the discrepancy and leaves it undone. It does not note the knock-on: a viewer gate added in session-core makes the gateway's hint always false, so in-place resume is never requested and no test would fail. Fix: decide now. Either keep the HTTP-edge allowlist as the meaning of 'service-readable' and record that, or add the gate together with a service-identity read in the gateway and a test that resumable arrives.

findings.file: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs (E, failure matrix) and session-core terminalization.rs
findings.issue: After a won pre-consume, deterministic failures that provably ran nothing leave the run paused with a spent approval, and recovery then fails the run. This covers connect refused, continue_disabled skew, resume_incomplete, authority_* and not_releasable. The committed ordinary path terminalizes immediately and tells the client it can retry, and the design deliberately drops that for continuations.
findings.evidence: The design leaves continue_unreachable un-terminalized by choice (open question 5) and admits the stranded click as a risk. I verified terminalization.rs has_pending_approval counts only approvals with consumed_at IS NULL, so a consumed approval does not spare the run. Recovery therefore ends the run Failed after the managed deadline. The executor's enforce_resume (continue_disabled, resume_incomplete) runs after the gateway has consumed, which is a new window the committed flow did not have. There is no mitigation beyond deploy order. Fix: at minimum a gateway-side check that the executor accepts a continuation before the consume, or an explicit decision that this window is accepted, with the recovery outcome stated as 'failed' rather than 'recovered'.

findings.file: apps/Model Plane/deploy and design section B (deploy order)
findings.issue: The deploy order (executor, then model-gateway, then BFF) leaves out session-core. The gateway's omit_call request and the fold_pause_consumed projection both need session-core first. With an old session-core the gateway still receives the decrypted tool arguments, which breaks the 'gateway holds no plaintext' invariant.

findings.issue: The consumed-approval predicate for resumable is justified as fixing a stale fold that stage 1 'leaves behind'. findings.evidence: run_agent_with_route at HEAD calls close_continued_pause after apply_authority for a resumed segment. findings.issue: omit_call does not skip the descriptor decrypt. store::consume_approval still runs read_consumed_call inside the transaction. blocking.file: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/terminalization.rs (claim_due_recovery, has_pending_approval, release_recovery_for_activity, run_recovery_worker) with S7c step 9 (gateway pre-consume)
blocking.issue: The pre-consume spends the click while the run's managed terminalization obligation still carries the stale deadline from the last pre-pause heartbeat. The recovery worker polls every second and treats an approval as pending only while consumed_at IS NULL. So the moment the gateway's ConsumeApproval commits, the run becomes eligible for recovery. Between the gateway consume and the executor's heartbeat_managed_agent_run, the worker can lease the row and terminalize the run as outcome_unknown. That window is gateway task spawn, RunAgent, executor auth, the executor's replay consume, close/claim RPCs, then the heartbeat. At HEAD the same window is in-process and milliseconds; S7c plus S7b widen it. For any approval taken more than 15 minutes after the pause, which is the normal human case, the stale deadline is already past. The design says recovery takes 'about 15 minutes' (failure matrix, risks, live proof s7-E 'budget 25'). That is false for a stale obligation: recovery runs within about 60 seconds of the consume. In the 'gateway died after consume', 'executor unreachable' and 'executor refused' rows the run is failed within about 60 seconds, not left paused. If the worker wins before the executor's replay, the replay is refused (NotFound) and nothing runs. If the worker wins after the replay but before the heartbeat, the executor never reads HeartbeatManagedRunResponse.already_terminal, so the approved call is dispatched on an already-terminal run. The user then sees a failed run with outcome_unknown although the effect ran, or a lost click.
blocking.evidence: claim_due_recovery selects obligations with state 'open', deadline_at <= now() and next_attempt_at <= now(), and excludes a run only when an approval is requested or granted with consumed_at IS NULL. release_recovery_for_activity only pushes next_attempt_at by ACTIVITY_RETRY_SECS (60) and leaves deadline_at untouched, so the deadline stays stale while the run waits. run_recovery_worker sleeps 1 s between passes. CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL sets consumed_at and does not touch the obligation. heartbeat_managed_agent_run in execution-core agent.rs returns Ok(()) and drops the response; grep for already_terminal in execution-core finds only test doubles.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a step to S7c's session-core slice. In the same transaction as the winning consume CAS in store::consume_approval (orchestration_store.rs), renew the server-owned managed obligation: UPDATE managed_run_terminalization_outbox SET state='open', deadline_at=now()+MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, next_attempt_at=now()+grace, lease fields NULL WHERE run_id=$ AND state IN ('open','processing'). That requires no producer token and gives every spent click a full grace window. Add an #[ignore] DB test a_consume_renews_the_recovery_deadline and a pure test that the SQL keeps the run_id predicate. Rewrite the failure-matrix, risk and live-proof timings to 'a full recovery window after the consume'. Record as a separate follow-up (S7b or S3) that the executor must stop when the heartbeat reports already_terminal, before any dispatch.

blocking.file: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/sse.rs (agentic_run_stream new continuation arms, continue_failure_event) and the chat.run.continue contract
blocking.issue: The design says every frame code means the approval is spent and the client must not retry with a new token. That is true only after a won gateway consume (resume switch on). With the resume switch off, which the design says leaves the RPC sequence unchanged, the executor refuses before its own consume for continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, Unauthenticated, PermissionDenied and a connect failure, so the approval is still granted and unconsumed. The three 'corrections apply regardless' remove terminalization and turn those cases into retryable:false frames with a contract that forbids retry. Nothing then ends the run: has_pending_approval spares any requested or granted approval with consumed_at NULL forever and ignores expires_at. The client is told not to retry, and the run sits in awaiting_approval with a usable approval. The committed code terminalized the run on a confirmed rejection or a connect failure, so this is also a behaviour change when the switch is off, contrary to the claim of byte-identical behaviour.
blocking.evidence: design sections E and F ('every frame code means the approval is spent'; effect table 'every frame code: spent, retryable false, followRun true'). blocking.suggested_fix: Make the frame vocabulary honest about spend state. Either (a) emit a separate not-spent code set, or a field approval_spent, when the gateway did not pre-consume, or (b) apply the typed non-terminalizing arm and the 'spent' contract only when the pre-consume ran, and keep the committed arms for the switch-off path. Alternatively state explicitly in the contract that with the switch off an executor refusal before consume leaves the approval usable and permits a retry with a new claim token. Add a test pairing each frame code with whether the approval is spent per switch state.

revised.slice: S7c - gateway and BFF half of the in-place resume, revision 2: /continue pre-consume (detached, spawn-testable, cancellation-safe) with a recovery-deadline renewal inside the consume transaction, resume_mode_for over RunDetail.resumable, closed HTTP and stream refusal vocabularies, continuation failure classification gated by the pre-consume attestation (no gateway terminalization of a pre-consumed continuation; committed arms untouched otherwise), no approved-plan consumption, BFF closed-code relay, chat.run.continue contract, three-part build order (S7c-0 / S7c-A / S7c-B after S7b), live-proof stages for S7
revised.summary: Revision 2 of the S7c design against HEAD 2aafc0b5. All six review findings were verified against committed source and all six hold. (1) CRITICAL, confirmed: claim_due_recovery selects open obligations with deadline_at <= now() and next_attempt_at <= now() and spares a run only while an approval is requested/granted with consumed_at IS NULL; CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL sets consumed_at and never touches managed_run_terminalization_outbox; release_recovery_for_activity moves only next_attempt_at; the worker polls every second; only heartbeat_managed_agent_run renews deadline_at (MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS = 15 min, mirrored here) and the executor ignores its already_terminal reply. So a spent click makes a run recoverable within about a second whenever the human took more than 15 minutes (the normal case); the same window exists at HEAD in stage 1 but is milliseconds long, pre-consume widens it to the whole gateway-to-executor path. Fix: a spend-only consume (wire field omit_call) renews the run's obligation in the SAME transaction as the winning compare-and-set (same statement shape as the heartbeat, scoped by run_id and org_id, states open/processing only), so every spent click gets a full 15-minute window measured from the consume; it also skips the descriptor decrypt entirely. The renewal is tied to spend-only so the executor's own consume (switch-off path) is byte-identical. Recorded follow-up outside S7c: the executor must stop when the heartbeat reports already_terminal. (2) HIGH, confirmed: with the resume switch off the executor refuses before its own consume (continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, auth, connect), so the approval is still granted; the first design made typed non-terminalizing retryable:false frames apply to every continuation, which both changed committed behaviour (the committed InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied and connect-refused arms terminalize) and told clients a usable approval was spent. Fix: the new arms are gated on the attestation (resume.consumed_by_gateway), not on resume.is_some(); a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keeps the committed arms byte for byte; every new frame carries approval_spent:true and the contract states the two regimes. (3 and 5) HIGH, confirmed by grep: loop_resume_enabled, LOOP_RESUME_ENV and AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway do not exist at HEAD (AgentResume ends at segment_no = 8, reserved 9). The build is split: S7c-0 and S7c-A need nothing from S7b; S7c-B (continue_resume arity, the loop_resume_enabled() call, the attestation arm, contract tests, compose) has the hard precondition that S7b's proto field, loop_resume_enabled() and the executor honouring the attestation have landed. (4) HIGH, confirmed: prepare_resume in execution-core runtime_loop/agent.rs is the only Rust ConsumeApprovalRequest struct literal and has no ..Default::default(), so omit_call = 7 breaks execution-core; an explicit omit_call: false hunk lands in the same commit as the proto edit (owner: the lead's proto commit, S7b is also editing that function). (6) HIGH, confirmed: consume_then_launch borrows its consumer and cannot spawn, and the planned drop test passes without a spawn. Fix: spawn_consume_then_launch owns the consumer, holds the only tokio::spawn and returns a oneshot receiver; the test drops the receiver while the consumer is parked mid-RPC and the server side still commits; a source scan requires continue_run to call spawn_consume_then_launch( (never consume_then_launch( directly) and the helper to contain tokio::spawn(, with a durable_loop_contract guard and mutation. Kept from the first design: the order of checks, the closed vocabularies, the plan-grant decision (a continuation never reads or claims it), the BFF closed relay, the contract-before-UI rule, the consumed-approval predicate for RunDetail.resumable, and the live-proof ladder (now with a stale-deadline stage). No file was edited and nothing was run that mutates anything; fold.rs, agent.rs and loop_checkpoint.rs edits in flight were not read.
revised.approach:
VERIFIED AGAINST COMMITTED SOURCE (HEAD 2aafc0b5; git show HEAD:path semantics, the in-flight fold.rs / agent.rs / loop_checkpoint.rs edits not read).

0. VERDICTS ON THE SIX FINDINGS
 F1 (recovery race) CONFIRMED and also true at HEAD for stage 1 (milliseconds there). Evidence by function: claim_due_recovery (candidate: state open AND deadline_at <= now() AND next_attempt_at <= now(), run not terminal, NOT EXISTS approval requested/granted with consumed_at IS NULL); has_pending_approval (same predicate, no expires_at test); release_recovery_for_activity (next_attempt_at only); run_recovery_worker (1 s sleep); CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL and store::consume_approval (never touch the outbox); heartbeat_managed_agent_run in the gateway-facing session-core (renews deadline_at = now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, state open, lease cleared, WHERE run_id AND state IN open/processing) versus the executor call site that discards the response. Fix in section I. The first design's 'recovery takes about 15 minutes' was false for a stale obligation and is rewritten: it is 15 minutes FROM THE CONSUME once section I lands.
 F2 (spent-state honesty) CONFIRMED. Committed behaviour for a continuation: InvalidArgument | Unauthenticated | PermissionDenied terminalize through terminalize_agent_dispatch_rejection_authenticated (frame agent_dispatch_rejected), a connect-phase Unavailable terminalizes as Unreachable (frame agent_dispatch_unreachable, retryable true), everything else is the degraded arm (agent_dispatch_unavailable). With the switch off those executor refusals happen BEFORE the executor's consume (enforce_resume, interceptors), so the approval is granted and unconsumed. Fix in section E: gate on the attestation.
 F3/F5 (build order) CONFIRMED by grep (no hit for consumed_by_gateway, loop_resume_enabled, LOOP_RESUME_ENV, EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED outside docs). Fix: three-part build order in steps.
 F4 (omit_call breaks execution-core) CONFIRMED: prepare_resume builds pb::ConsumeApprovalRequest with six explicit fields and no struct update; no Go literal exists outside gen/. Fix: explicit hunk.
 F6 (detach not protected) CONFIRMED by construction: consume_then_launch(&C, request, launch) cannot spawn, nothing is awaited between the consumer's answer and launch(), so the first design's drop test is vacuous. Fix in section B.

A. ORDER OF EVERY RPC AFTER S7c (resume switch on; with it off see the last paragraph)
 BFF: mint model, data-plane, inference, execution, session bearers (auth-core); org ZDR read; POST gateway /continue.
 Gateway: 1 continuation_gate (local). 2 continue_persistent_gate (local; ZDR and waived refused 409 not_resumable before anything is read). 3 body check (400 continue_incomplete). 4 bearer check (401 missing_bearer). 5 require_durable_run_owner_with_token (session-core). 6 GetRun (status, goal, thread_id, resumable). 7 GetApproval. 8 continue_preflight (local, refuses a consumed approval; no consume yet). 9 ONE detached task (spawn_consume_then_launch): ConsumeApproval with the user bearer (the same VerifiedModelBearer the executor later forwards as its session bearer; verified: spawn_run_dispatch is handed &model_bearer), step_id '', action_fingerprint '', claim_token as sent, omit_call true; session-core in ONE transaction: compare-and-set, renew the run's managed obligation (section I), commit; response consumed true. Only on consumed == true the task calls the launch closure (agentic_run_stream with the attested continue_resume). The handler awaits a oneshot. 10 inside the stream task: 'connected' frame; NO approved-plan claim; spawn_run_dispatch -> RunAgent; orchestration tail. 11 executor (S7b): enforce_resume, ConsumeApproval replay (same claim; reads the descriptor; consumed=false, already_consumed, same_claim; accepted because the attestation says the gateway sent exactly one RunAgent per won consume), then stage 1 or the in-place claim path, then heartbeat.
 Resume switch off (EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED unset at the gateway): steps 1-8 unchanged; step 9 is just launch() (agentic_run_stream with mode 'segment', consumed_by_gateway false, no pre-consume, no spawn); step 10 loses only the approved-plan claim (section D); step 11 as committed. The failure arms are the committed ones (section E). Exceptions to byte identity, stated honestly: (a) no plan claim and no plan block in goal when a plan is pending on the thread (a defect fix, shippable as the separate commit S7c-0), (b) the BFF relays closed codes instead of model_error for the gateway's 409/404. The RPC sequence to session-core's approval store and to execution-core is otherwise the committed one.

B. PRE-CONSUME RULES AND THE DETACHED TASK
 Answer map (pure fn preconsume_refusal(Result<bool, tonic::Status>) -> Result<(), PreconsumeRefusal>): Ok(true) proceed. Ok(false) (already consumed, whatever the claim, the SAME token included) -> 409 continuation_already_consumed (standing default: refuse every consumed approval). NotFound -> 404 approval_not_found. FailedPrecondition approval_not_granted | approval_expired | approval_not_resumable -> 409 same code; any other FailedPrecondition -> 409 not_resumable. InvalidArgument -> 400 continue_incomplete. PermissionDenied | Unauthenticated -> crate::http_routes::grpc_status_to_http (same as the owner check and reads). Unavailable | DeadlineExceeded | Internal | Unknown | Cancelled | Aborted | ResourceExhausted -> 503 continue_unavailable (ambiguous: the consume may have committed; on Internal from a failed renewal the transaction rolled back, still reported as ambiguous because the client cannot tell). Upstream messages are never echoed; logs carry the gRPC code and run_id only.
 Plaintext: the request sets omit_call = true; session-core then does not decrypt the descriptor at all (store spend-only intent, section I), returns consumed/already_consumed/same_claim only (consume_response also drops any call defensively). The gateway reads exactly one field, .consumed.
 Detach (finding 6): trait ApprovalConsumer { fn consume(&self, ConsumeApprovalRequest) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, tonic::Status>> + Send }. struct GrpcApprovalConsumer owns an OrchestrationCoreServiceClient<Channel> clone (state.orchestration_client.clone()) and an owned VerifiedModelBearer clone (verified Clone), no borrows. async fn consume_then_launch<C: ApprovalConsumer, T>(consumer: &C, request, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal> stays the pure sequencing unit. fn spawn_consume_then_launch<C, T>(consumer: C, request: ConsumeApprovalRequest, launch: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<Result<T, PreconsumeRefusal>> where C: ApprovalConsumer + Send + 'static, T: Send + 'static is the ONLY place with tokio::spawn: it creates the oneshot, spawns an async move block that runs consume_then_launch(&consumer, request, launch).await and sends the outcome (ignoring a closed receiver), returns the receiver. agentic_run_stream returns Sse<ReceiverStream<..>> (Send, 'static) and spawns its own dispatch task, so once launch returns, RunAgent no longer depends on the handler. If the receiver is dropped the Sse is dropped with it; the stream task's sends are already ignored (let _ = tx.send), so the dispatch continues (whether follow_agentic_run exits early on a closed client channel is UNVERIFIED; dispatch itself does not depend on it). continue_run builds ONE launch closure (the single agentic_run_stream call in the body) and: resume off -> Ok(launch()); resume on -> match spawn_consume_then_launch(..).await { Ok(Ok(sse)) => Ok(sse), Ok(Err(Closed(s,c))) => continue_error, Ok(Err(Status(st))) => grpc_status_to_http, Err(_closed) => continue_error(503, continue_unavailable) }.
 Deploy order: executor image (S7b attestation honoured) first, then session-core (omit_call and renewal), then model-gateway, then flip EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED on both. New gateway with an old executor and the ledger off spends the click and fails with continuation_already_consumed. Gateway on with session-core old: omit_call is ignored by an old server, the response then carries the call (the gateway still reads only .consumed, but the decrypted call crosses to the gateway: deploy session-core first).

C. MODE CHOICE
 resume_mode_for(resume_enabled: bool, resumable: bool) -> &'static str: 'loop' only when both, else 'segment'; these two literals are the only place a mode is named. No other value is ever sent; segment_no stays 0; step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint, brief stay empty. The hint is advisory: the executor decides at claim time; a wrong hint costs a fallback to stage 1, never a refusal. Hint accuracy: session-core RUN_SELECT gains fold_pause_consumed = EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM approvals a WHERE a.run_id = r.id AND a.org_id = r.org_id AND a.idempotency_key = lc.pause_ref AND a.consumed_at IS NOT NULL); row_to_detail: resumable = old rule AND NOT (fold kind 'pause' AND fold_pause_consumed). pause_ref and approvals.idempotency_key are both format!(\"{run_id}:{step_id}\") (a DB test pins the pairing). park_reason is not read by S7c. Verified at HEAD: row_to_detail returns resumable to any viewer who can read the run and park_reason only to owner/service (RunDetail fields 17 and 18); run_detail_value in model-gateway http_routes is an allowlist without either (test-pinned here). DISCREPANCY kept open: at RPC level resumable is not owner-gated.

D. THE THREAD'S APPROVED PLAN: A CONTINUATION NEVER TOUCHES IT
 plan_context_wanted(plan_mode, resuming) = !plan_mode && !resuming gates approved_plan_context in agentic_run_stream. A /continue never calls take_approved_plan, never claims the plan, never injects it into goal, never reads granted_rung (dispatch_autonomy_rung(resuming) already states no rung). Reason: the approval pending on a thread belongs to a later execute turn; in-place ignores req.goal so a claim burns the single-use grant, stage 1 would inject it into a run that never held it. Consequence: the grant keeps its TTL for the next ordinary run. This applies to every continuation regardless of the switch (defect fix; shippable alone as S7c-0).

E. FAILURE CLASSIFICATION, GATED BY THE ATTESTATION (finding 2)
 let preconsumed = resume.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| r.consumed_by_gateway). The new arms apply only when preconsumed. Rationale: only then is the approval provably spent when the stream opens (the pre-consume won), so only then is 'no retry with a new token' true; and only then would a gateway terminalization be able to kill a run another segment owns. With preconsumed false, every arm is the committed one, byte for byte (terminalize on InvalidArgument/Unauthenticated/PermissionDenied and on connect refused; agent_dispatch_unavailable otherwise), and the approval stays usable exactly as today.
 For preconsumed: pure classify_continue_dispatch_failure(&tonic::Status) -> ContinueDispatchFailure { Refused(&'static str), Unreachable, Unknown }: Refused(token) when the code is NotFound (always approval_not_found), FailedPrecondition, Aborted, InvalidArgument, PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated and the message is in CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS; an unknown message there -> Refused(continue_refused) (never echoed); Unreachable = dispatch_never_reached_execution_core; Unknown = every other status, the follow deadline, a join error. Frames via continue_failure_event(request_id, run_id, &ContinueDispatchFailure) -> Event: ChatEvent::Error { code, message = code with spaces, retryable: false }, payload gains run_id and approval_spent: true. Refused(token) -> that token; Unreachable -> continue_unreachable; Unknown -> continue_outcome_unknown; local request-construction failure -> continue_refused. No terminalization in any of them. RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED is still published for Unreachable and Unknown, not for Refused. Placement: an arm Ok(Ok(Err(status))) if preconsumed BEFORE is_confirmed_agent_dispatch_rejection; the three agent_dispatch_unavailable_event sites become dispatch_unknown_event(preconsumed, ..) (false returns the old frame); the Err(error) construction branch gets a preconsumed early path before its terminalization.
 What a pre-consumed continuation leaves behind and who ends it: the run is non-terminal, the approval is spent, and the managed obligation was renewed at the consume (section I), so session-core recovery terminalizes it 15 minutes after the consume if nothing heartbeats. Hence the failure matrix and live proof timings are 15 minutes FROM THE CONSUME.

F. CLIENT-VISIBLE VOCABULARIES (closed, test-pinned, owned by the gateway)
 HTTP, CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS (10): continue_disabled(409), not_resumable(409), continue_incomplete(400), missing_bearer(401), approval_not_found(404), approval_not_granted(409), approval_expired(409), approval_not_resumable(409), continuation_already_consumed(409), continue_unavailable(503). BFF relays 8 (all but continue_incomplete, which its own guard preempts, and missing_bearer, which maps to unauthorized). Owner-check and read failures keep grpc_status_to_http's flat body (BFF model_error). With the switch off, 409 continuation_already_consumed also arises from continue_preflight as at HEAD.
 Stream, CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS (19): executor-sourced continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, continuation_already_consumed, approval_not_found, approval_not_granted, approval_expired, approval_not_resumable, approval_action_mismatch, approval_snapshot_mismatch, not_releasable, authority_widened, authority_space_mismatch, authority_route_mismatch, continue_space_scope_unsupported, continue_in_progress, resume_checkpoint_unavailable; gateway-made continue_refused, continue_unreachable, continue_outcome_unknown. These frames exist ONLY for a pre-consumed continuation and always carry approval_spent: true. Meaning: the approval is spent (by this request); no retry with a new claim token; follow the run through its events. continue_space_scope_unsupported and the authority_* tokens are unreachable through the gateway today (Space/pinned approvals are cold; the gateway states no wider authority) and stay as defence in depth. Frames agent_dispatch_unavailable / agent_dispatch_rejected / agent_dispatch_unreachable on a continuation (switch off) make NO claim about the approval and the contract says so (a retry with a new token is then permitted by the committed rules).

G. BFF
 proxy_sse_stream_with_data_plane (upstream.rs; verified: its status >= 400 branch today returns model_error, 401 -> unauthorized) gains a trailing relayed_errors: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)] (code, fixed message). The two upstream wrappers and chat/shared.rs (2 sites) and chat/streams.rs (1 site) pass &[]; orchestration.rs continue_run passes CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS. The branch: 401 -> unauthorized unchanged, else return upstream_error_response(resp, status, relayed_errors).await, a free function outside the relay body so tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs keeps scanning an unchanged byte path. Empty list: today's model_error without reading the body. Non-empty: read at most 4096 bytes, parse {error:{code}}, relay only a code in the list with the list's own message and the upstream status; flat string body, unlisted code, malformed or oversized stays model_error. Upstream messages are never relayed.

H. SPA CONTRACT (rule: contract before any UI wiring; none wired)
 The error vocabulary the client sees changes (model_error to closed codes), so chat.run.continue is updated first: new module src/shared/actions/chat-run-continue-contract.ts with the HTTP tuple (8 relayed), the frame tuple (19), chatRunContinueRefusalOf(input) (accepts ApiError-like {code,status} or an SSE error frame body {code, approval_spent}) and a per-code effect table. Two regimes written into it: a frame whose code is in the frame tuple and carries approval_spent true means spent, retryable false, followRun true; any other frame (including agent_dispatch_*) says nothing about the approval. HTTP effects: approvalSpent 'no' except continuation_already_consumed 'by_another' and continue_unavailable 'unknown'. The descriptor description states single use, closed refusals, no retry with a new token after a spent frame, and that the thread's plan grant is untouched. The input schema (runId, approvalId, claimToken) is pinned unchanged; continueRun keeps its signature; no UI caller is added.

I. RECOVERY DEADLINE RENEWAL AT THE CONSUME (finding 1)
 session-core store: new pub async fn consume_approval_spend_only(pool, id, org_id, run_id, user_id, action_fingerprint, claim_hash) and the existing consume_approval become two thin wrappers over a private consume_approval_with(.., intent: ConsumeIntent { Full, SpendOnly }) (the existing 7-argument consume_approval and its ~20 #[ignore] test call sites stay untouched). In SpendOnly: on the winning branch, before commit, run RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL: UPDATE managed_run_terminalization_outbox SET state = 'open', deadline_at = now() + ($3::bigint * interval '1 second'), next_attempt_at = now(), lease_owner = NULL, lease_token_hash = NULL, lease_expires_at = NULL, updated_at = now() WHERE run_id = $1 AND org_id = $2 AND state IN ('open', 'processing'), bound to MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS (terminalization.rs const made pub(crate), a one-word hunk). Zero rows affected is not an error (a run without an obligation). The descriptor is not read or decrypted in SpendOnly (call None) on either the winning or the replay branch. A database error rolls the whole transaction back, so the click is not spent. Only a WON spend-only consume renews (a replay or a lost race never extends a deadline). orchestration_grpc.rs consume_approval picks the intent from req.omit_call and builds the response through pure consume_response(done, omit_call). Lock order: the consume transaction locks the approval row then the outbox row and does not lock runs; recovery locks the run row then the obligation: no cycle. Effect: after a won pre-consume the obligation is open with deadline now + 15 min, the worker cannot claim it for 15 minutes, a 'processing' lease held earlier is cleared so recover_claimed_terminalization's state check fails safe. Abuse bound: one extension per consumed approval, owner-only. NOT in S7c (recorded follow-up, owner S7b or S3): the executor must stop when HeartbeatManagedRunResponse.already_terminal is true, before any dispatch (verified: the call site discards the response; already_terminal appears only in test doubles). Open: renew on the executor's own full consume as well (hardens HEAD stage 1 but changes the switch-off path).

J. CONSEQUENCES OF THE DECIDED DEFAULTS
 Refuse every consumed approval: a retry with the same token after a dropped connection is 409 continuation_already_consumed; recovery is the run's events, the unknown-outcome closers or the 15-minute recovery from the consume (S8 later). Waived runs: refused at continue_persistent_gate before anything is read. Widened request refused not narrowed: the gateway states nothing wider (no rung, floor 0, plan false, no Space, no route). Writer requires the ledger and a failed pre_effect save holds effects: nothing for the gateway; the live proof needs the ledger on.

WHAT S7c NEEDS FROM S7b (the interface both designs must fit)
1. AgentResume.mode: only 'segment' (stage 1) and 'loop' (stage 2); the stage is chosen only by this field. The gateway sends 'loop' only with its switch on and RunDetail.resumable. The executor downgrades 'loop' to stage 1 when its own switches (resume, checkpoint) are off, as a downgrade, never a refusal. segment_no is 0 and ignored; step_id, tool_name, action_fingerprint, brief empty.
2. AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway (bool, field 10, add-only, owned and honoured by S7b, set by S7c exactly when the gateway pre-consumed). Rule for BOTH stages: replay_ok = resume.consumed_by_gateway || effect::ledger_enabled(); proceed when consumed.consumed || (consumed.already_consumed && consumed.same_claim && replay_ok); otherwise continuation_already_consumed. Safe because the gateway sends exactly one RunAgent per won consume (no retry layer on the gateway's execution channel was found; unverified beyond a source read) and a duplicate /continue never reaches RunAgent (409 at the pre-consume). Honoured whatever the executor's resume switch says. Fallback if S7b refuses the field: make EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED mandatory wherever the gateway's resume switch is on.
3. Refusal tokens the executor may return after a consume, as gRPC code plus exact message: FailedPrecondition continuation_already_consumed | approval_not_granted | approval_expired | approval_not_resumable | approval_action_mismatch | approval_snapshot_mismatch | not_releasable | authority_widened | authority_space_mismatch | authority_route_mismatch | continue_space_scope_unsupported | resume_checkpoint_unavailable | continue_disabled; Aborted continue_in_progress; InvalidArgument resume_incomplete; NotFound (session-core text) for a vanished approval. Anything else reaches the client as continue_refused: safe, unhelpful; a new token needs a row in CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS and the contract test. A claim failure after a won consume is a fallback to stage 1, not a refusal (S7b), except the fatal ones above.
4. Every refusal returns from run_agent_with_route BEFORE heartbeat_managed_agent_run, finalize or any terminal write and leaves the run non-terminal and the managed obligation untouched. continuation_already_consumed from the replayed released step (after phase 2) is the one refusal that may arrive with another segment running: the gateway relies on this rule not to kill that run (it does not terminalize an attested continuation).
5. Content-free closed log fields as live-proof evidence: resume_stage (in_place | stage_one) and fallback_reason (the RestoreFailure token) on one line per continuation, no ids beyond run_id.
6. S7b adds mp_contracts::loop_fold::LOOP_RESUME_ENV and loop_resume_enabled() (via switch_from; absent at HEAD) and the execution-core compose entry; S7c only calls loop_resume_enabled().
7. NEW: S7b may rely on the managed obligation having been renewed to now + 15 minutes at a spend-only consume, so no recovery lease can fire between the gateway's consume and the executor's heartbeat. S7b (or S3) owns the follow-up that stops the executor when HeartbeatManagedRunResponse.already_terminal is true before any dispatch.
WHAT S7b CAN RELY ON FROM S7c: a won ConsumeApproval with the same claim_token already happened (the replay returns the descriptor and authority to the claimant only; a replay is a full consume, omit_call false, and does not renew); the request states neutral placeholders (mode 'ask', no rung, floor 0, plan false, no Space, no route, no tools, goal = the run's goal, max_rounds from the gateway env); segment_no 0; the thread's plan and grant were not touched.

risks: STRANDED CLICK (the price of pre-consume): any failure after a won consume and before the executor consumes or claims (gateway crash, executor unreachable, executor refusal, version skew) leaves the approval spent and the run paused until the renewed recovery window ends (15 minutes after the consume, once section I lands; without it, about a second after the consume for a stale obligation, which is why section I is a requirement, not an option). A retry is 409 by the standing decision. Mitigation: deploy order and flipping both switches together; S8 or a park TTL is the real recovery.

Section I changes session-core's consume path: a won spend-only consume now writes to managed_run_terminalization_outbox. Lock order was checked (approval then outbox; recovery takes run then obligation, the consume does not lock runs) but only by source read; the DB tests are written, not run. A deadlock or a renewal that misses (zero rows) must not fail the consume; zero rows is accepted, a database error rolls back the consume.

Deploy skew with omit_call: an old session-core ignores the field, so the decrypted call would come back to the gateway (which reads only .consumed but still receives it) and no renewal would run. Deploy session-core before the gateway; the S7c-B contract guard cannot see deployment order.

Attestation dependency: without AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway (or a mandatory ledger) pre-consume breaks /continue with the ledger off. S7b must land first and keep the rule independent of its own resume switch. Gateway on and executor continue switch off now refuses AFTER the gateway spent the click (new hazard of pre-consume).

The executor still ignores HeartbeatManagedRunResponse.already_terminal (pre-existing at HEAD): a run terminalized by any other path is still dispatched. Section I removes the pre-consume-specific race, not the underlying defect. Follow-up recorded for S7b or S3.

has_pending_approval has no expires_at test (pre-existing, redteam gap): a granted-but-unconsumed approval spares its run from recovery forever. A refused pre-consume (409 approval_expired and similar) therefore leaves the run exactly as it was before. Out of S7c scope.

With the switch off, differences on a dormant route remain: the plan-grant correction (no plan claim, no plan block in goal) and the BFF relaying closed codes instead of model_error. Shippable as S7c-0 ahead of everything if the lead wants strict identity for the rest.

The detached task decouples the consume from the client connection but a gateway process crash between the consume RPC and the RunAgent send is not covered; honest residual window (recovered by the renewed deadline).

Handler-drop behaviour on disconnect is hyper's: the unit test proves the detach through spawn_consume_then_launch and the source guard proves continue_run uses it, not the runtime. UNVERIFIED end to end, including whether follow_agentic_run returns early on a closed client channel.

Adding a trailing parameter to the 16-argument BFF relay touches the chat callers (3 sites plus 2 wrappers) with no behaviour change; a second relay function would duplicate the byte path guarded by sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs.
Contract guard churn: durable_loop_contract.rs anchors mutations on literal text of continue_resume; re-pointing is a review hot spot and each guard must stay able to fail.

The hint predicate reads approvals by idempotency_key = pause_ref; if S6 stops keying the pause approval as run:step the predicate silently stops excluding consumed folds (costs a fallback, never safety); a DB test pins the pairing.
ConsumeApproval's RunResumedAfterApproval broadcast now fires at the gateway's consume (before dispatch); the executor's replay does not re-broadcast. Run-console consumers see it earlier.

invariants: The gateway consumes an approval at most once per /continue: only after every refusal check, only for a persistent turn, only with EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED on; only a won consume (consumed == true) proceeds; every other answer, the same claim token included, is 409 continuation_already_consumed.

Consume and launch are one detached task owned by spawn_consume_then_launch (the only tokio::spawn of the path): a client disconnect cannot spend an approval without RunAgent being sent. Test- and source-guarded.

A won spend-only consume renews the run's managed obligation deadline in the same transaction (open, deadline now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, lease cleared); a replay, a lost race or a full consume never renews. A spent click always has a full recovery window.

The gateway never holds a consumed call's content: omit_call is set, session-core does not decrypt or return it, one boolean is read, and logs carry the gRPC code and run_id only, never the claim token, an approval id's content or an upstream message.

The gateway never terminalizes an attested (pre-consumed) continuation; the new arms are gated on consumed_by_gateway, and a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keeps the committed arms byte for byte.

Every continuation frame carrying a code from CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS also carries approval_spent true and retryable false; a frame without it (agent_dispatch_* on a switch-off continuation) makes no claim about the approval.

The mode the gateway sends is 'loop' only with the switch on and RunDetail.resumable, else 'segment'; no other value; segment_no 0; hint fields empty; a wrong hint costs a stage-1 fallback and nothing else.
A continuation never reads, claims or injects the thread's approved plan or grant and states no rung, floor, Space, route or tools.
resumable and park_reason never reach a browser (run_detail_value is an allowlist); a pause fold whose approval is consumed is not resumable.

The BFF relays only a (status, code) pair from the closed list with its own fixed message; every other upstream error is model_error or unauthorized; SSE bytes are relayed untouched and the relay body still passes tests/sse_relay_no_allowlist.rs.

The executor, not the gateway, owns what a continuation runs: tools, authority, mode and the approved call come from the paused snapshot; the executor's consume replay is the only reader of the descriptor.

With EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED off, the RPC sequence to session-core's approval store and to execution-core and the RunAgent bytes of /continue are the committed ones, with the two stated exceptions (no plan claim, BFF code relay).
One /continue route, one AgentResume literal (continue_resume), one segment_no literal, one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal in the gateway, one agentic_run_stream call in continue_run.
The workspace builds after every commit: the omit_call proto field and the execution-core literal land together; S7c-B lands only after S7b's symbols exist.
No bearer, token or claim token is persisted or logged; the vocabularies contain closed tokens only.
open_questions: Attestation vs ledger: pre-consume needs the executor to accept a same-claim replay with the ledger off. This design uses AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway = 10 (S7b honours it). Accept, or make EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED mandatory wherever the gateway's resume switch is on (no proto field, a deployment coupling)?

Gating: pre-consume, the loop stage, the attestation and now the typed-frame arms are tied to EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, so switch-off identity holds and stage-1-only deployments keep the old 200-plus-error-frame race. Tie the pre-consume to AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED instead (closes the race for stage 1 too, but a rolling deploy with an old executor and the ledger off then spends clicks)?

omit_call: add the ConsumeApprovalRequest field (gateway never holds plaintext, session-core never decrypts, Go regen needed) or decode and drop? This design takes the field because the renewal also keys on it.
Should the executor's own full consume (the switch-off stage-1 path) also renew the recovery deadline? That would harden HEAD's millisecond window but changes the switch-off path; default here: no.

Ambiguous consume (503 continue_unavailable) and the dropped-connection case both end in 409 on retry by the standing decision. Still the ruling for a TRANSPORT-ambiguous consume, or may the gateway accept a same-claim replay only while the run is paused and no segment started (needs a durable 'segment started' fact that does not exist)?

Should continue_unreachable (connect refused: provably nothing ran) terminalize the run at once as dispatch_unreachable, as an ordinary run does, instead of leaving it to the renewed 15-minute recovery? Default: leave it, because the gateway never terminalizes an attested continuation and a skewed executor may be back in minutes.

Plan grant: confirm that a continuation never consumes the thread's approved plan and the grant stays for the next ordinary run; and whether that defect fix ships as the separate commit S7c-0 (default) or inside S7c.

resumable at session-core RPC level is returned to every reader of the run, only park_reason is owner/service gated. If 'service-readable only' means the RPC level, row_to_detail needs a viewer gate (s4 follow-up). Not changed here.
The consumed-approval predicate amends s4's ownership of the RunDetail projection by one condition. Confirm it lands in S7c-A rather than as an s4 follow-up commit.

Who owns the omit_call: false hunk in execution-core prepare_resume while other units edit agent.rs: default is the lead, in the same commit as the proto edit.

amendments_to_prior_specs: FIRST S7c DESIGN, recovery timing (finding 1, confirmed): 'recovery takes about 15 minutes' was false for a stale obligation. Replaced by a renewal of the managed obligation inside the winning spend-only consume transaction; timings in the failure matrix, risks and live proof are now '15 minutes from the consume'. The first design's claim that pre-consume only needed the attestation was incomplete: it also needed the renewal.

FIRST S7c DESIGN, section E and the 'corrections apply regardless' claim (finding 2, confirmed): the typed non-terminalizing frames no longer apply to every continuation. They apply only to a pre-consumed (attested) continuation and carry approval_spent: true; a continuation the gateway did not pre-consume keeps the committed dispatch arms byte for byte. 'Every frame code means the approval is spent' is narrowed to the frames that carry approval_spent. Of the three former 'corrections apply regardless' only the plan-grant fix and the BFF relay still apply with the switch off, and both are listed as exceptions to byte identity.

FIRST S7c DESIGN, steps order (findings 3 and 5, confirmed): the work is split S7c-0 / S7c-A / S7c-B; S7c-B (continue_resume arity, loop_resume_enabled call, attestation arms, contract guards, compose) has the hard precondition that S7b landed its proto field, loop_resume_enabled() and the attestation rule. Pure pieces that name no S7b symbol land first.

FIRST S7c DESIGN, file_changes (finding 4, confirmed): added the explicit omit_call: false hunk in execution-core runtime_loop/agent.rs prepare_resume, same commit as the proto edit; the first design listed no such hunk and said step 1 had no dependents.

FIRST S7c DESIGN, detach (finding 6, confirmed): consume_then_launch borrowed its consumer and could not spawn, so the drop test was vacuous. Added spawn_consume_then_launch (owned consumer, the only tokio::spawn, oneshot return), a mid-RPC drop test, and a source scan plus a durable_loop_contract guard with a mutation that deletes the spawn.

FIRST S7c DESIGN, omit_call semantics: the first design had session-core still decrypt the descriptor and drop it from the response. Now a spend-only consume skips the decrypt on both branches (store intent), and the same intent is what triggers the renewal. consume_approval keeps its exact 7-argument signature through a thin wrapper, so the ~20 existing store tests are untouched.
FIRST S7c DESIGN, interfaces to S7b: added item 7 (S7b may rely on the renewed obligation) and the recorded follow-up that the executor must stop when the heartbeat reports already_terminal.

S7 spec (earlier) section A/F (consume order, loser of a race): an executor-side consume that is a same-claim replay no longer comes for free; the committed stage-1 rule (replay_is_fenced = ledger on) refuses it with the ledger off, so the gateway pre-consume requires the AgentResume.consumed_by_gateway attestation.

S7 spec section F: 'two parallel calls with the SAME token: both pass consume, the executor's claim refuses the second with claim_held, a 200 stream whose first frame is continue_in_progress'. Superseded: the second request gets 409 continuation_already_consumed at the pre-consume (standing decision: refuse every consumed approval, same token included). continue_in_progress becomes a stream-only token, unreachable through the gateway with the switch on.

S7 spec section F mapping and BFF list: continue_in_progress was listed as an HTTP code; corrected, it is a stream frame code. The HTTP relay is exactly 8 codes; the gateway adds 503 continue_unavailable for an ambiguous consume.

S7 spec 'BFF: no action contract change' is reversed. The error vocabulary the client sees changes (model_error to closed codes, plus typed stream frames with approval_spent), so chat.run.continue and a new contract module are updated first; still no UI caller.

S7 spec sections G/H: EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED at the gateway only chose the mode. It now also gates the pre-consume, the attestation, the spawned task and the typed-frame arms (through the attestation), so with it off the continue route is the committed one apart from the two stated exceptions.
S7 spec section G: resumable semantics gain one predicate: a pause fold whose approval is consumed is not resumable, so the stale fold a stage-1 continuation leaves behind stops advertising itself.

S7 spec risk 'Gateway pre-consume widens the gateway's role ... nothing new is persisted': refined: the gateway receives no call content (omit_call, no decrypt) and the consume now persists one thing, the renewed recovery deadline.

Reconcile 'Gateway /continue pre-consume' (404 approval_not_found, 409 for the rest): kept, plus 503 continue_unavailable for transport-class failures, 400 for InvalidArgument, passthrough for PermissionDenied and Unauthenticated, and typed classification of everything the executor can return after the consume (attested continuations only).

Reconcile 'a real /continue also consumes the thread's pending approved plan': decided as no consumption by a continuation (plan_context_wanted), a defect fix in the committed S3 route, shippable as S7c-0.

S9 contract guard (durable_loop_contract.rs builder_and_validator_violations): the 'continue_resume builds a literal mode' regex and its mutation anchor are re-pointed to resume_mode_for; the segment_no and one-literal checks are unchanged. The gateway also gets exactly one ConsumeApprovalRequest literal, a spawn guard and an attestation-gate guard.
failure_matrix: BFF cannot mint a bearer (auth-core down) | nothing | existing delegated_auth_unavailable | nothing consumed; retry freely.
BFF cannot reach model-gateway | nothing | 502 upstream_unavailable | nothing consumed; the same token may retry.
Gateway: switch off, ZDR or waived turn, blank body, missing bearer | nothing read or written | 409 continue_disabled, 409 not_resumable, 400, 401 | nothing consumed.
Owner check, GetRun or GetApproval fails | nothing | grpc_status_to_http status with a flat body, BFF model_error | nothing consumed.

Preflight refuses (run ended, approval of another run, not granted, cold approval, already consumed) | nothing | 409 not_resumable | 404 approval_not_found | 409 approval_not_granted | 409 continuation_already_consumed | nothing consumed; for a consumed approval the other continuation owns it.

Pre-consume: another claim won first, or the same token again | the winner's state | 409 continuation_already_consumed | session-core compare-and-set; this request never reaches RunAgent; no renewal for the loser.
Pre-consume NotFound (run ended or lost retention between preflight and consume, approval gone) | nothing | 404 approval_not_found | the store's predicates; discloses nothing about the run.
Pre-consume FailedPrecondition not_granted, expired, not_resumable | nothing | 409 with that code | nothing consumed, nothing renewed.

Pre-consume transport failure or timeout | consumed_at possibly set (unknown), deadline possibly renewed | 503 continue_unavailable | nothing ran; if it committed the click is spent and a retry is 409; the run is non-terminal and recovery ends it 15 minutes after the consume (open question).

Pre-consume renewal statement fails (database error) | the whole consume transaction rolls back; the click is NOT spent | 503 continue_unavailable | the same token may retry; the gateway cannot tell this from a committed consume, so it reports ambiguity.

Client disconnects during the consume RPC | consume possibly committed | nobody (client gone) | spawn_consume_then_launch finishes the consume and still launches RunAgent; the continuation runs; the user reconnects through run events; a retry is 409.

Gateway process dies after the consume committed, before RunAgent is sent | consumed_at set, deadline renewed to consume + 15 min, paused fold untouched, run non-terminal | broken connection (BFF 502 or transport event) | nothing ran; retry is 409; recovery terminalizes about 15 minutes after the consume and purges the fold (before section I: within a second for a stale obligation, the finding-1 defect). Honest residual window.

Recovery worker polls between the consume and the executor heartbeat | nothing | nothing | the renewed deadline makes the run ineligible for 15 minutes, so the executor's replay and heartbeat always find a live run (finding 1).

RunAgent request cannot be built locally after a pre-consume | spent, nothing ran | frame continue_refused, retryable false, approval_spent true | not terminalized; recovery 15 minutes after the consume. (Not pre-consumed: the committed terminalizing arm.)

Executor unreachable (connect refused), pre-consumed | spent, nothing ran, run non-terminal | frame continue_unreachable, retryable false, approval_spent true | RUN_DISPATCH_DEGRADED published; recovery 15 minutes after the consume; retry is 409. Not pre-consumed (switch off): committed arm, run terminalized, agent_dispatch_unreachable retryable true, approval still unconsumed.

RunAgent outcome ambiguous (reset after send, follow deadline, join error), pre-consumed | the continuation may be running | frame continue_outcome_unknown, retryable false, run_id, approval_spent true | do not retry; follow the run; the executor owns the receipt; closers and sweep decide unknown effects; no gateway terminalization. Not pre-consumed: committed agent_dispatch_unavailable.

Executor refuses before dispatching (any token in the 19), pre-consumed | spent, run non-terminal, fold unchanged (or resuming for its lease) | frame with that token, approval_spent true | nothing ran; executor returns before heartbeat or any terminal write (S7b rule 4); recovery after the renewed window.

Executor refuses before its own consume, NOT pre-consumed (switch off: continue_disabled, resume_incomplete, auth) | approval granted and unconsumed | the committed frame (agent_dispatch_rejected with the run terminalized, or agent_dispatch_unavailable) with no approval_spent | committed behaviour, byte for byte; a retry with a new claim token is allowed by the committed rules (finding 2).

Executor returns continuation_already_consumed after phase 2 (released step replayed), pre-consumed | another segment owns and runs the run | frame continuation_already_consumed | the gateway does not terminalize: the attested arm precedes the confirmed-rejection arm; the committed arm would have failed a live run.
Executor returns continue_in_progress (claim held, same token) | the first continuation is alive | frame | unreachable through the gateway with the switch on (the second request is 409 earlier).
Executor completes | normal frames and done | the answer | one released ledger row under the new step id; executor heartbeat renews the deadline as at HEAD.

Executor pauses again | new approval (step ids prefixed with the next segment) | awaiting_approval frame | a fresh /continue with the new approval and a new claim token; the fold exists only if the in-place writer is seeded.
Browser disconnects mid-stream after dispatch | run continues server side | nothing | RunAgent task is detached; the thread shows the result.
BFF loses the upstream mid-stream | run continues | existing upstream_unavailable event | unchanged.
Two clicks at once, distinct tokens | one winner | one 200 stream and one 409 | the CAS; one ledger row for the released call; one renewal.
Two clicks at once, same token | one winner | one 200 and one 409 (new) | pre-consume refuses the loser; closes the same-token gap.
Approved plan pending on the thread | untouched | nothing | the continuation never takes it.

Gateway switch on, executor continue switch off | spent click | frame continue_disabled, approval_spent true | deploy and flip both together; the executor refuses in enforce_resume after the gateway spent the click (new hazard of pre-consume); recovery 15 minutes after the consume.
Gateway resume switch on, executor resume switch off | none | normal | executor downgrades loop to stage 1; the attestation is honoured regardless.

Executor resume switch on, gateway off | none | normal | the committed behaviour: the executor consumes itself, no attestation, no renewal beyond the executor's own heartbeat (millisecond window as at HEAD).
New gateway with an old executor, ledger off | spent click | frame continuation_already_consumed, approval_spent true | do not deploy in that order; executor first.

New gateway with an old session-core | omit_call ignored, call returned to the gateway (read as .consumed only), no renewal | normal | deploy session-core before the gateway; the stale-deadline window is back until it is.

Stale fold after a stage-1 continuation | the original pause fold stays until terminal purge | later continues use 'segment' | the consumed-approval predicate makes resumable false; a wrong 'loop' would cost one claim_not_claimable fallback.

Executor does not stop on heartbeat already_terminal (pre-existing) | a run terminalized by another path can still have its approved call dispatched | the user sees a failed run although the effect ran | not caused by S7c, narrowed by the renewal; follow-up recorded for S7b or S3.
